薩桑多琴源自印尼東努沙登加拉羅地島，名稱來自羅地方言詞，意為振動或發聲樂器；當地: The sasando comes from Rote Island in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia; the name comes from a word in the Rote dialect meaning a vibrating or sounding instrument, and local tradition holds that it existed by the seventh century. The origin legend tells of a boy, Sangguana, who dreamed of the instrument under a palm tree and on waking made it from palm leaves and strings as he remembered, which became the story of the instrument. Over the past century the sasando and similar bamboo-tube string instruments have taken up new materials such as metal wire and tuning pegs, but the structure that uses dried palm leaves as a resonator remains an important feature.
薩桑多琴為管狀齊特琴，發聲來自竹管上張弦；木楔使弦高於管面，並以不同弦長產生不同: The sasando is a tubular zither, its sound coming from strings stretched on a bamboo tube; wooden wedges raise the strings above the surface of the tube, and different string lengths give different pitches. The player puts both hands through the opening at the front and plucks, in a way similar to the harp or the kacapi. Its resonator is a fan of dried palm leaves wrapped round the bamboo tube, and the character of the sound depends on the string lengths, the height of the wedges and the resonance of the leaf fan. The source records only 28-string and 56-string versions and gives neither the range nor the way the volume is controlled. Compared with other tubular zithers, the sasando directs its sound with the leaves; the others are mostly of bamboo, originally with strings cut from bamboo, some now using wire and tuning pegs, but none with this leaf fan.
薩桑多琴的主體為竹管，用作琴框；竹管周圍設數片木楔，用以固定弦線並拉出不同有效弦: The body of the sasando is a bamboo tube that serves as the frame; several wooden wedges around the tube hold the strings and pull out different sounding lengths. The resonator is the fan of dried palm leaves wrapped round the tube, which the source calls the resonator. The string material is not clearly stated in this passage of the source, which mentions only, when comparing other tubular zithers, that some instruments (the sasando among them) have changed to wire and tuning pegs, so it is not clear whether all the strings are wire. The source adds nothing about the materials of the other parts.
薩桑多琴（Sasando）是印尼東努沙登加拉羅地島的傳統弦鳴樂器，屬管狀齊特琴，: The sasando is a traditional chordophone of Rote Island in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, a tubular zither that looks and is plucked much like a harp. The body is a bamboo tube, wooden wedges round it hold the strings so that different lengths give the pitches, and the tube is wrapped in a fan-shaped resonator of dried palm leaves. The player puts both hands through the opening at the front and plucks with the fingers. The people of Rote use it for traditional music, and its name comes from the Rote words for "vibrate" or "sound".
